title: Supported integral coefficients, rationalization and norm inclusion
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $\Omega$ be a normed field with a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra structure, and let $E\subset\Omega$ be an intermediate field finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\mathcal O_E$ be the integral coefficient ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], equipped with its subspace topology in $E$. All continuous-function coefficient rings are those of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], bundled as commutative coefficients of [def-sfb-condensed-point-modules-geometric-base-change]. Put
$$O=C(-,\mathcal O_E),\qquad A=C(-,E),\qquad B=C(-,\Omega).$$
The latter two are the norm coefficient rings of [def-sfb-field-action-geometric-transport-data]. Define $\mathrm{supportedLatticeIntegralRing}(\ell,E)=O$. Define the rationalization $O\to A$ and norm inclusion $A\to B$ by postcomposition with the actual inclusions $\mathcal O_E\hookrightarrow E$ and $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$, respectively [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. These use all continuous functions, not only functions taking values in a finite subextension.

Let $K$ be a field, let $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be a finite-type scheme, let $a:S\hookrightarrow T$ be a locally closed immersion, and let $L_0\in\mathrm{Modules}(O,S)$, with notation from [def-sfb-condensed-point-modules-geometric-base-change]. The finite-type hypothesis makes $T$ Noetherian. Using the actual canonical locally closed extension $a_!$ of [def-sfb-locally-closed-coefficient-extension], the pulled-back coefficients $O_T,A_T$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and ordinary internal scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], define the supported rationalized lattice
$$\mathrm{supportedRationalizedLattice}(\ell,E,T,a,L_0)=Q:=\bigl(A_T\otimes_{O_T}a_!L_0\bigr)[0]\in D(\mathrm{Modules}(A,T)),$$
where degree zero and the ordinary unbounded derived category use [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. All fields and schemes lie in universe $u$, coefficient groups in $u+1$, and derived localization in $u+2$. The construction is defined for every $L_0$; its lisse specialization uses [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. No completeness of $\Omega$, flatness of $A\to B$, nonempty support or positive rank is imposed.

For a scheme $T$, the norm point projection $B\otimes^L_A\mathcal H_A(-)\to\mathcal H_B(B_T\otimes^L_{A_T}-)$ attached to these coefficients is the pointProjection of [def-sfb-field-action-geometric-transport-data] along the norm inclusion $A\to B$, formed with the canonical point scalar comparison $\mathrm{canonicalPointScalar}(A\to B,T)$ of [def-sfb-canonical-point-scalar-comparison]: the transpose of insertion of $1$ followed by the canonical comparison with exact scalar restriction, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

def supportedRationalizedLattice (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    {Ω : Type u} [NormedField Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[ℓ] Ω]
    (E : IntermediateField ℚ_[ℓ] Ω) [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    {K : Type u} [Field K] (T : Over (Spec (.of K)))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType T.hom] [QuasiCompact T.hom]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (a : S ⟶ T.left) (ha : IsImmersion a)
    (L₀ : Modules (supportedLatticeIntegralRing ℓ E).toMon S) :
    DerivedCategory.{u + 2} (Modules (normCoefficients E).toMon T.left)
lean.note: Owns only the four existing plain definitions, including the actual rationalization and norm inclusion maps and degree-zero Q construction. It does not assert the supported-lattice projection isomorphism. Reuses the existing locally closed coefficient extension and arbitrary normed-field coefficients; no Lean source is changed. The norm point projection used with these coefficients is the existing pointProjection with canonicalPointScalar, owned by def-sfb-canonical-point-scalar-comparison (cited; reviewer fix).
